Link families the preview reads

The readers of _EXT_READERS, in order: the first that takes a link reads it. “Any window”: its links open in place in every window. “All links”: every link a reader takes opens in place in its own window.

  • 1 On its own site a detail link opens in the site's own window; it needs that site's preview switch (Brucebase shows also sa_bb_event_preview).
  • 2 Needs sa_pop_mb (Preview linked entities on hover). Off musicbrainz.org it is MusicBrainz's window read from the other site (dg-mb): its Web Service request anonymous, its Live page and editing history with the browser's musicbrainz.org cookies (vzell's consent: discogs.com and setlist.fm, then on 2026-11-03 the Springsteen sites and archive.org).
  • 3 setlist, artist and venue pages need sa_pop_ext_setlistfm_key; without it only /search?artist= is read, and on setlist.fm itself the others keep their new tab.
  • 4 On discogs.com a Discogs page no reader takes is the site's own link and keeps its new tab.
  • 5 Brucebase's own reader, under sa_bb_event_preview; with it off, the generic reader's (then here only in a window that opens every link).
⚑

Gaps

None open. Gaps found and fixed are recorded in org/non-MB-coverage.org.

Keeping it current

Generated from docs/non-mb-coverage.json by scripts/build-coverage-report.py, which also writes NON-MB-COVERAGE.org. --check fails when a site, pageType or reader exists in the userscript and not here, or the other way round, or when this page is stale.
